A.title: Make councils' £100m fund pay low-income homes in bands E to H
A.answer: Keep the £100 for bands A to D and the councils' £100 million fund. Change one rule. In 20 councils drawn by lot from volunteers, the fund must pay £100 to low-income homes in bands E to H, with no form, using benefit records the Department for Work and Pensions already holds. Other councils run the fund as now, so nobody gets less than today. Provisional fail number: fewer than 8 in 10 eligible homes paid by 31 March 2027. Stops 30 June 2027 unless Parliament votes to keep it. On a pass, the rule goes to every council. The Energy Secretary answers for it. It leaves out Scotland, Wales and low-income households not on benefits.

B.title: Let local panels, not councils alone, steer the £100m help fund
B.answer: Try this in 10 volunteer English councils, drawn by lot. A local panel of residents and advice workers would decide who gets the council's share of the £100 million fund. It would put low-income homes in bands E to H first, with a short, simple claim. Other councils keep today's rules. The main £100 payment stays as planned. By 31 May 2027, measure days to payment and how much reaches bands E to H, against places like it. Provisional fail: fewer than 7 in 10 approved claims paid within 30 days. It stops on 31 May 2027 unless Parliament votes to keep it. The Energy Secretary answers for it. It leaves out Scotland and Wales.
